title: Choctaw code talkers of the First World War
summary: Choctaw soldiers of the US 142nd Infantry relayed battlefield messages in their own language from October 1918, inventing terms such as 'big gun' for artillery.
why: Held by the Choctaw Nation to be the first Native American code talkers in the US military.

notes.problem: Source attributes the 'first' claim to the Choctaw government, not as established fact.

unsung.contribution: Sent coded battlefield messages in Choctaw that the enemy could not decipher.
unsung.recognition: Little was said or written of them after the war; France honoured them in 1989 and Congress in 2008.
